title: Exploring Mixtures and their Separation: Chapter Introduction
summary: Muddy water settles but milk never does: particle size decides how a mixture behaves. Solutions, colloids and suspensions, and the ways to separate them.

notes.title: 00 – Exploring Mixtures and their Separation: Chapter Introduction

keyPoints: Most materials around us are **mixtures**: air, sea water, milk, soil.
**Solution**: particles < 1 nm, invisible, never settle (salt water).
**Suspension**: particles > 1000 nm, visible, settle under gravity (muddy water).

**Colloid**: 1-1000 nm, do not settle but scatter light, the **Tyndall effect** (milk). Separation methods match the mixture: filtration, evaporation, chromatography, distillation, magnetic separation.

quiz.q: Milk does not settle on standing because it is a:
quiz.explain: Its particles are mid-size: they do not settle but scatter light.

quiz.q: Muddy water settles because its particles are:
options: Large enough for gravity to pull them down
quiz.explain: Suspension particles are big and settle.

quiz.q: The Tyndall effect is seen in:
quiz.explain: Colloid particles scatter a light beam.

quiz.q: Iron filings mixed with sand are best separated by:
quiz.explain: Iron is attracted by a magnet; sand is not.
